course.title: First Aid Basics
course.tagline: Handle cuts, burns, choking and emergencies calmly until help arrives.

days.title: First aid: what it is and when to use it
days.goal: Learn what first aid is and the first thing to do in an emergency.

video.title: Hands-Only CPR Instructional Video

steps: Watch the video and write down what first aid means in your own words.
Learn the first rule: check the scene is safe before you help.
Learn the emergency number in your area and write it down.
Tell a friend the emergency number from memory.
days.task: Write the emergency number on a card and keep it in your wallet.
days.challenge: Say the emergency number out loud 5 times from memory.

quiz.q: What is first aid?
options: Help given to a hurt person before doctors arrive
quiz.explain: First aid is early help until experts arrive.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to do at an emergency?
quiz.explain: A safe scene protects you and the hurt person.

quiz.q: Why learn the emergency number?
options: So you can call for help fast
quiz.explain: Knowing the number saves time in an emergency.

days.title: Stay calm and check the person
days.goal: Learn how to stay calm and check if a person responds.

video.title: Using an AED by American Red Cross

steps: Learn DRABC: Danger, Response, Airway, Breathing, Circulation.
Tap the person's shoulder and ask loudly: Are you OK?
If they answer, ask what hurts.
Practise the shoulder tap and question with a friend.
days.task: Practise checking response with a friend.
days.challenge: Write DRABC on a card and learn what each letter means.

quiz.q: What does DRABC stand for?
quiz.explain: DRABC is the order to check a hurt person.

quiz.q: How do you check if a person responds?
options: Tap their shoulder and ask: Are you OK?
quiz.explain: A gentle tap and a loud question checks response.

quiz.q: Why stay calm in an emergency?
options: Calm thinking helps you act clearly
quiz.explain: Staying calm helps you help well.

days.title: Call for help the right way
days.goal: Learn what to say when you call the emergency number.

video.title: BLS - Choking Video

steps: Say where you are: the address and a clear landmark.
Say what happened in short words.
Say how many people are hurt.
Stay on the line until they tell you to hang up.
days.task: Practise an emergency call with a friend playing the operator.
days.challenge: Write your home address on a card by your phone.

quiz.q: What should you say first in an emergency call?
quiz.explain: Your location helps help find you fast.

quiz.q: Why say how many people are hurt?
options: So the right help is sent
quiz.explain: Numbers help send enough help.

quiz.q: When should you hang up?
options: When the operator tells you to
quiz.explain: Staying on the line lets the operator guide you.

days.title: CPR: hands only, step by step
days.goal: Learn hands-only CPR for an adult who is not breathing.

video.title: How to Help a Choking Adult

steps: Check response: tap and shout.
Call the emergency number or ask someone else to call.
Push hard and fast in the centre of the chest: 100 to 120 pushes a minute.
Keep going until help arrives or the person wakes up.
days.task: Practise the hand position on a cushion.
days.challenge: Practise pushing to the beat of a song at 100 beats a minute.

quiz.q: When do you start CPR?
options: When a person does not respond and is not breathing normally
quiz.explain: CPR is for a person who is not breathing.

quiz.q: Where do your hands go in CPR?
options: In the centre of the chest
quiz.explain: The centre of the chest is the right spot.

quiz.q: How fast should you push?
quiz.explain: One hundred to 120 a minute keeps blood moving.

days.title: Use an AED safely
days.goal: Learn what an AED is and how to use one.

video.title: How to Help a Choking Infant

steps: An AED is a machine that shocks the heart back to a normal beat.
Turn it on and follow its voice prompts.
Stick the pads on the person's bare chest as shown.
Stand back when it says to, and let it work.
days.task: Find where the nearest AED is in your area.
days.challenge: Practise the AED steps out loud with a friend.

quiz.q: What is an AED?
options: A machine that shocks the heart back to a normal beat
quiz.explain: An AED helps restart a heart that stopped.

quiz.q: What should you do when the AED says stand back?
options: Move away and let it work
quiz.explain: Standing back keeps you safe during a shock.

quiz.q: Where should the pads go?
options: On the bare chest as shown on the pads
quiz.explain: Pads on bare skin work correctly.

days.title: Stop bleeding from a cut
days.goal: Learn how to stop bleeding from a cut.

video.title: Basic First Aid

steps: Press a clean cloth firmly on the cut.
Keep pressing until the bleeding slows.
Raise the cut part above the heart if you can.
Cover with a clean bandage and get help if bleeding does not stop.
days.task: Practise pressing a cloth on a pretend cut.
days.challenge: Check your first aid kit for clean cloths and bandages.

quiz.q: What is the first step for a bleeding cut?
options: Press a clean cloth firmly on it
quiz.explain: Firm pressure slows bleeding.

quiz.q: Why raise the cut part?
options: It slows blood flow to the cut
quiz.explain: Raising the part above the heart slows bleeding.

quiz.q: When should you get more help?
options: If bleeding does not stop after pressing
quiz.explain: Bleeding that will not stop needs medical help.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 1: Your first aid kit
days.goal: Put week 1 together: build a home first aid kit.

video.title: First Aid Tips: Treating Minor Injuries at Home

steps: Get a box or bag for your kit.
Add: clean cloths, bandages, plasters, gloves, scissors, tape.
Add the emergency number card.
Put the kit where everyone in the house can find it.
days.task: Build your first aid kit and show it to your family.
days.challenge: Teach a family member where the kit is.

quiz.q: What should a first aid kit have?
options: Cloths, bandages, plasters, gloves, scissors, tape
quiz.explain: A kit needs basics to treat small injuries.

quiz.q: Where should you keep the kit?
options: Where everyone can find it fast
quiz.explain: A kit must be easy to reach in an emergency.

quiz.q: Why add gloves to a kit?
quiz.explain: Gloves protect you when helping a bleeding person.

project.title: Your first aid kit
project.brief: Build a home first aid kit with cloths, bandages, plasters, gloves, scissors and tape, plus an emergency number card, and show your family where it is.
checks: Emergency number card is in the kit
Showed the family where it is

days.title: Treat a small burn
days.goal: Learn how to treat a small burn safely.

video.title: How Do You Treat a Choking Adult? New 2020 AHA / ILCOR Guidelines

steps: Cool the burn with cool running water for 10 minutes.
Do not use ice, butter or toothpaste.
Cover loosely with a clean cloth or cling film.
Get help if the burn is large or on the face.
days.task: Practise the burn steps out loud.
days.challenge: Check your kitchen for a clean cloth to use.

quiz.q: What is the first step for a small burn?
options: Cool it with running water for 10 minutes
quiz.explain: Cool water eases pain and stops the burn going deeper.

quiz.q: Why not use ice on a burn?
options: Ice can damage the skin further
quiz.explain: Ice can harm burnt skin.

quiz.q: When should you get help for a burn?
options: If it is large, deep or on the face
quiz.explain: Large or face burns need medical care.

days.title: Help a choking adult
days.goal: Learn how to help an adult who is choking.

video.title: How to Help a Choking Adult or Child | Back Blows, Abdominal Thrusts, and Chest Thrusts

steps: Ask: Are you choking? If they can cough, let them cough.
If they cannot breathe, give 5 back blows between the shoulder blades.
Then give 5 belly pushes: hands above the belly button, pull in and up.
Repeat until the food comes out or help arrives.
days.task: Practise back blows and belly pushes on a cushion.
days.challenge: Teach a friend the steps in order.

quiz.q: What is choking?
options: Food stuck in the throat blocking air
quiz.explain: Choking blocks the airway so air cannot pass.

quiz.q: What should you do first?
options: Ask if they are choking and let them cough if they can
quiz.explain: Coughing can clear the blockage on its own.

quiz.q: Where do belly pushes go?
options: Above the belly button, pulling in and up
quiz.explain: Belly pushes push air up to clear the blockage.

days.title: Help a choking child
days.goal: Learn how to help a choking child safely.

video.title: The Recovery Position - First Aid Training - St John Ambulance

steps: For a small child, lay them face down on your forearm.
Give 5 gentle back blows between the shoulder blades.
Turn them over and give 5 gentle chest pushes.
Call for help if the blockage does not clear.
days.task: Practise the steps on a doll or cushion.
days.challenge: Write the steps on a card for your fridge.

quiz.q: Why are child choking steps gentler?
options: Children are smaller and more fragile
quiz.explain: Gentle blows suit a small body.

quiz.q: Where do back blows go?
quiz.explain: Back blows between the shoulders help clear the blockage.

quiz.q: When should you call for help?
options: If the blockage does not clear
quiz.explain: A blockage that will not clear needs help fast.

days.title: Treat a sprain
days.goal: Learn how to treat a sprained ankle or wrist.

video.title: Hands-Only CPR Instructional Video

steps: Rest the hurt part and stop using it.
Put ice wrapped in a cloth on it for 15 minutes.
Wrap it lightly with a bandage for support.
Raise it up on a pillow.
days.task: Practise wrapping a bandage on your ankle.
days.challenge: Write the 4 steps: rest, ice, wrap, raise.

quiz.q: What is a sprain?
options: A stretched or torn ligament in a joint
quiz.explain: A sprain hurts a joint's ligament.

quiz.q: What does RICE stand for?
quiz.explain: RICE is rest, ice, wrap and raise.

quiz.q: Why wrap a sprain?
options: To support the joint and reduce swelling
quiz.explain: A light wrap supports the joint.

days.title: Treat a nosebleed
days.goal: Learn how to stop a nosebleed.

video.title: Using an AED by American Red Cross

steps: Sit down and lean forward a little.
Pinch the soft part of the nose for 10 minutes.
Breathe through your mouth.
Do not tilt your head back.
days.task: Practise the steps with a friend.
days.challenge: Write the steps on a card.

quiz.q: Why lean forward during a nosebleed?
options: So blood does not go down the throat
quiz.explain: Leaning forward stops blood going down the throat.

quiz.q: How long should you pinch the nose?
quiz.explain: Ten minutes lets the blood clot.

quiz.q: Why not tilt your head back?
options: Blood would go down the throat
quiz.explain: Tilting back sends blood down the throat.

days.title: Help someone who fainted
days.goal: Learn what to do when someone faints.

video.title: BLS - Choking Video

steps: Lay them on their back and raise their legs a little.
Loosen tight clothes around the neck.
Check they are breathing.
If they do not wake up soon, call for help.
days.task: Practise the steps with a friend.
days.challenge: Write the steps on a card.

quiz.q: What is fainting?
options: Passing out for a short time
quiz.explain: Fainting is a brief loss of consciousness.

quiz.q: Why raise the legs?
options: It helps blood flow back to the brain
quiz.explain: Raised legs help blood reach the brain.

quiz.q: When should you call for help?
options: If they do not wake up soon
quiz.explain: A long faint needs medical help.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 2: Your emergency plan
days.goal: Put week 2 together: write a home emergency plan.

video.title: How to Help a Choking Adult

steps: Write the emergency number and your address on one page.
Write where your first aid kit is.
Write the steps for CPR, choking and bleeding.
Show the plan to your family and practise once.
days.task: Write your emergency plan and show your family.
days.challenge: Practise one step from the plan with a family member.

quiz.q: What should an emergency plan have?
options: Numbers, address, kit location and key steps
quiz.explain: A plan puts the key facts in one place.

quiz.q: Why practise the plan?
options: So you act fast when it is real
quiz.explain: Practice turns panic into calm action.

quiz.q: Who should know the plan?
quiz.explain: Everyone should know where the kit is and what to do.

project.title: Your emergency plan
project.brief: Write a home emergency plan with the emergency number, your address, the kit location and the key steps for CPR, choking and bleeding.
checks: Showed the plan to your family

days.title: CPR for a baby
days.goal: Learn how CPR is different for a baby.

video.title: How to Help a Choking Infant

steps: Use two fingers in the centre of the baby's chest.
Push down gently, about 4 cm deep.
Give 30 pushes, then 2 gentle breaths.
Keep going until help arrives.
days.task: Practise the two-finger position on a doll.
days.challenge: Write the baby CPR steps on a card.

quiz.q: How is baby CPR different?
options: It is the same as adult CPR
You do not do CPR on babies
You use two fingers and push gently
quiz.explain: A baby's chest needs gentle two-finger pushes.

quiz.q: How deep should you push on a baby?
quiz.explain: About 4 cm is right for a baby.

quiz.q: How many pushes before breaths?
quiz.explain: Thirty pushes then two breaths is the pattern.

days.title: Treat a cut that needs stitches
days.goal: Learn how to tell if a cut needs a doctor.

video.title: Basic First Aid

steps: Press a clean cloth on the cut.
If the cut is deep, wide or will not stop bleeding, go to a doctor.
Do not put cotton wool in a deep cut.
Cover with a clean bandage for the trip.
days.task: Practise pressing a cloth on a pretend deep cut.
days.challenge: Write the signs that mean see a doctor.

quiz.q: What cut needs a doctor?
options: A deep, wide cut or one that will not stop bleeding
quiz.explain: Deep or non-stop bleeding needs a doctor.

quiz.q: Why not put cotton wool in a deep cut?
options: Fibres can stick in the wound
quiz.explain: Cotton fibres can stay in the wound.

quiz.q: What should you do on the way to the doctor?
options: Keep pressing a clean cloth on the cut
quiz.explain: Pressure keeps bleeding slow.

days.title: Help with a broken bone
days.goal: Learn what to do if you think a bone is broken.

video.title: First Aid Tips: Treating Minor Injuries at Home

steps: Do not move the hurt part.
Support it with a pillow or rolled cloth.
Put ice wrapped in a cloth on it if you can.
Call for help or take the person to a doctor.
days.task: Practise supporting a pretend broken arm with a pillow.
days.challenge: Write the steps on a card.

quiz.q: What is the first rule for a broken bone?
options: Do not move the hurt part
quiz.explain: Moving a broken bone can make it worse.

quiz.q: How should you support it?
options: With a pillow or rolled cloth
quiz.explain: Soft support keeps the bone still.

quiz.q: What should you do next?
options: Call for help or go to a doctor
quiz.explain: A broken bone needs medical care.

days.title: Treat a sting or bite
days.goal: Learn how to treat an insect sting or bite.

video.title: How Do You Treat a Choking Adult? New 2020 AHA / ILCOR Guidelines

steps: Move away from the insect.
Wash the sting with soap and water.
Put a cold cloth on it to ease pain and swelling.
Get help fast if the person cannot breathe or swells a lot.
days.task: Practise the steps out loud.
days.challenge: Check your kit for a cold cloth or ice pack.

quiz.q: What is the first step for a sting?
quiz.explain: Moving away stops more stings.

quiz.q: Why wash the sting?
quiz.explain: Washing stops germs getting in.

quiz.q: When should you get help fast?
options: If the person cannot breathe or swells a lot
quiz.explain: Trouble breathing after a sting is an emergency.

days.title: Help with heatstroke
days.goal: Learn the signs of heatstroke and what to do.

video.title: How to Help a Choking Adult or Child | Back Blows, Abdominal Thrusts, and Chest Thrusts

steps: Signs: very hot skin, confusion, headache, no sweating.
Move the person to a cool, shady place.
Cool them with wet cloths and fan them.
Call for help at once.
days.task: Practise the steps out loud.
days.challenge: Write the signs of heatstroke on a card.

quiz.q: What is heatstroke?
quiz.explain: Heatstroke is dangerous overheating.

quiz.q: What is a sign of heatstroke?
quiz.explain: Hot skin and confusion mean heatstroke.

quiz.q: What should you do first?
options: Move them to a cool, shady place
quiz.explain: Cool shade is the first step.

days.title: Help with a seizure
days.goal: Learn what to do when someone has a seizure.

video.title: The Recovery Position - First Aid Training - St John Ambulance

steps: Stay calm and time the seizure.
Move hard objects away from the person.
Do not hold them down or put anything in their mouth.
When it stops, lay them on their side and call for help if it lasts over 5 minutes.
days.task: Practise the steps out loud with a friend.
days.challenge: Write the steps on a card.

quiz.q: What is a seizure?
options: Sudden shaking and loss of control of the body
quiz.explain: A seizure is sudden uncontrolled shaking.

quiz.q: What should you NOT do during a seizure?
options: Hold them down or put things in their mouth
quiz.explain: Holding down or putting things in the mouth can hurt them.

quiz.q: What should you do after a seizure?
quiz.explain: Lying on the side keeps the airway clear.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 3: Practise a full emergency
days.goal: Put week 3 together: run a practice emergency from start to finish.

video.title: Hands-Only CPR Instructional Video

steps: Pick a scenario: a friend falls and cuts their leg.
Check the scene, check response, call for help.
Stop the bleeding with a cloth and bandage.
Write down what you did well and what to fix.
days.task: Run the practice emergency with a friend.
days.challenge: Write down what went well and what to fix.

quiz.q: What comes first in any emergency?
quiz.explain: A safe scene protects everyone.

quiz.q: What should you do after stopping the bleeding?
options: Keep the person calm and wait for help
quiz.explain: Staying calm and waiting keeps them safe.

quiz.q: Why write down what went well?
options: So you can improve next time
quiz.explain: Notes help you get better.

project.title: Practise a full emergency
project.brief: Run a practice emergency from start to finish: check the scene, check response, call for help, stop bleeding, and write what went well.
checks: Wrote what went well and what to fix

days.title: First aid for sports injuries
days.goal: Learn the common sports injuries and their first aid.

video.title: Using an AED by American Red Cross

steps: Cuts: press with a clean cloth.
Sprains: rest, ice, wrap, raise.
Nosebleeds: sit, lean forward, pinch.
Heat: move to shade, cool down, drink water.
days.task: Practise one sports injury step today.
days.challenge: Pack a small sports first aid kit.

quiz.q: What is the first aid for a sprain?
quiz.explain: RICE treats sprains.

quiz.q: What should a sports kit have?
quiz.explain: A sports kit needs basics for common injuries.

quiz.q: Why carry water to sport?
options: To replace sweat and cool the body
quiz.explain: Water keeps players safe in heat.

days.title: Check your kit and your skills
days.goal: Check your first aid kit and test your skills.

video.title: BLS - Choking Video

steps: Open your kit and check every item.
Throw out anything old or used up.
Replace what is missing.
Test yourself: name the steps for CPR and choking.
days.task: Check and restock your kit today.
days.challenge: Name the CPR steps from memory.

quiz.q: How often should you check your kit?
quiz.explain: Regular checks keep the kit ready.

quiz.q: What should you do with old items?
options: Throw them out and replace them
quiz.explain: Old items may not work when needed.

quiz.q: Why test yourself?
quiz.explain: Testing keeps skills ready for a real emergency.

days.title: Stay calm under pressure
days.goal: Learn how to stay calm when someone is hurt.

video.title: How to Help a Choking Adult

steps: Take one slow breath before you act.
Say out loud what you are doing: I am checking the scene.
Do one step at a time.
Ask someone nearby to help you.
days.task: Practise saying your steps out loud.
days.challenge: Practise a slow breath before acting.

quiz.q: Why take a slow breath first?
options: It calms you so you can think clearly
quiz.explain: One slow breath stops panic.

quiz.q: Why say your steps out loud?
options: It keeps you focused and tells others what you need
quiz.explain: Saying steps out loud keeps you calm and clear.

quiz.q: What should you do if you feel panicked?
options: Breathe slowly and do one step at a time
quiz.explain: Slow steps beat panic.

days.title: Teach first aid to your family
days.goal: Teach your family the basics of first aid.

video.title: How to Help a Choking Infant

steps: Show them where the kit is.
Teach them the emergency number.
Teach them how to stop bleeding from a cut.
Practise a call for help together.
days.task: Teach one family member the emergency number.
days.challenge: Show your family the kit today.

quiz.q: Why teach your family?
options: So anyone can help in an emergency
quiz.explain: A family that knows first aid is safer.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to teach?
options: The emergency number and the kit location
quiz.explain: Numbers and kit location are the basics.

quiz.q: Why practise together?
options: So everyone acts fast when it is real
quiz.explain: Practice makes the family ready.

days.title: Help someone who is panicking
days.goal: Learn to help a person who is panicking.

video.title: Basic First Aid

steps: Stay calm and speak slowly.
Help them sit down.
Breathe with them: in for 4 counts, out for 4 counts.
Tell them they are safe.
Do not crowd them.
If it does not pass, call for help.
days.task: Practise slow breathing with a friend.
days.challenge: Write down the 4 steps to help a panicking person.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to do?
quiz.explain: Your calm voice helps them feel safe.

quiz.q: How should you breathe with them?
options: In for 4 counts, out for 4 counts
quiz.explain: Slow steady breathing calms the body.

quiz.q: When should you call for help?
options: If the panic does not pass
quiz.explain: If slow breathing does not help, get help.

days.title: Keep a first aid kit in your car
days.goal: Learn what to keep in a car first aid kit.

video.title: First Aid Tips: Treating Minor Injuries at Home

steps: Put a small kit in your car.
Add bandages, gloves, a torch and a blanket.
Check it every 3 months.
Keep a charged phone.
Write emergency numbers on a card.
Tell your family where the kit is.
days.task: Make a car first aid kit list.
days.challenge: Check your car kit this week.

quiz.q: What should a car kit have?
options: Bandages, gloves, a torch and a blanket
quiz.explain: Bandages, gloves, a torch and a blanket cover most small emergencies.

quiz.q: How often should you check it?
quiz.explain: Checking every 3 months keeps supplies fresh.

quiz.q: Why keep a charged phone?
options: So you can call for help
quiz.explain: A charged phone lets you call for help anywhere.

days.title: Get ready for your capstone
days.goal: Review the whole course and prepare your final test.

video.title: How Do You Treat a Choking Adult? New 2020 AHA / ILCOR Guidelines

steps: Read your notes from weeks 1 to 4.
List 5 skills you can now do.
Practise CPR and choking steps once more.
Write down any questions you still have.
days.task: List 5 first aid skills you learned.
days.challenge: Practise CPR steps from memory.

quiz.q: What is the capstone?
options: A final test that shows what you learned
quiz.explain: The capstone is your final show of skill.

quiz.q: What should you review before the capstone?
options: Your notes from all four weeks
quiz.explain: Reviewing all weeks brings the course together.

quiz.q: How do you know you are ready?
options: You can do the key steps calmly from memory
quiz.explain: Calm, correct steps show you are ready.

days.title: Final practice day
days.goal: Practise your capstone once more, then rest.

video.title: How to Help a Choking Adult or Child | Back Blows, Abdominal Thrusts, and Chest Thrusts

steps: Run a practice emergency from start to finish.
Check your kit one more time.
Fix anything that felt rushed.
Rest well tonight.
days.task: Run a practice emergency and time each part.
days.challenge: Fix one thing that felt rushed.

quiz.q: Why practise once more?
options: Practice makes the real run calm and smooth
quiz.explain: Practice turns worry into calm confidence.

quiz.q: What should you check after practice?
options: Your steps, your timing and your kit
quiz.explain: Checking steps and kit makes you ready.

quiz.q: What should you do the night before?
quiz.explain: Good rest helps you do your best.

days.title: Capstone day: handle an emergency
days.goal: Show what you learned: handle a practice emergency from start to finish.

video.title: The Recovery Position - First Aid Training - St John Ambulance

steps: Check the scene is safe.
Check response and call for help.
Give the right first aid for the injury.
Write a short report on what you did.
days.task: Handle the practice emergency and write your report.
days.challenge: Hand in your report and celebrate.

quiz.q: What is the first step in any emergency?
quiz.explain: A safe scene protects everyone.

quiz.q: What should you do after giving first aid?
options: Stay with the person until help arrives
quiz.explain: Staying keeps the person safe.

quiz.q: What goes in your report?
options: What you did and what you learned
quiz.explain: A short report shows what you learned.

capstone.title: Handle an emergency calmly
capstone.brief: Handle a practice emergency from start to finish: check the scene, check response, call for help, give the right first aid, stay with the person, and write a short report.
checks: Called for help with clear facts
deliverables: A short video or notes from the practice
